sections.h2: What kind of county is Pike County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Pike County is a small, fast-growing county south of metro Atlanta with Zebulon as its seat. The Census Bureau counted 18,889 residents in April 2020 and estimated 20,932 for July 2025, a rise of 10.8% in about five years.

The county covers 216.09 square miles of land, which works out to 87.4 people per square mile in 2020. Many residents commute out of the county: mean travel time to work is 35.7 minutes, the longest of the four Georgia counties in the same Census comparison. Pike also has few renters. Owners live in 84.6% of occupied housing, so most sales here are houses that a family has owned and lived in for years.

The county's tax commissioner works from 79 Jackson Street in Zebulon, and the City of Zebulon's own site says Pike County collects city property tax on the city's behalf. A seller inside the city limits therefore deals with one office for the bill.

sections.h2: What do Pike County home values and incomes look like?
sections.html:
Pike has the highest home values of any county in this group of four. The 2020-2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $305,600, against a median household income of $86,719.

Those costs help explain why tax bills matter to a Pike seller: a higher home value means a larger assessment, and the county's building permits (106 in 2025) show that new houses keep arriving to compete with yours.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Pike County?
sections.html:
Two county offices share the work, and neither one sets your millage rate. The assessor values the property, and the tax commissioner sends and collects the bill.

  • Tax Commissioner: 79 Jackson Street, Zebulon, (770) 567-2001, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. This office bills and collects county, school and state tax and handles mobile home and timber tax. It also takes payments through pikecountypay.com.
  • Board of Tax Assessors: (770) 567-2002. This office takes returns, homestead applications and appeals, and answers questions about value.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: keeps the deed room in the Pike County Courthouse, where you can get a copy of your warranty deed, and where a tax lien (FIFA) is recorded if bills go unpaid.
  • Board of Commissioners and Board of Education: adopt the millage rates each year.

The tax commissioner's site states that the bill goes to the owner and is never mailed to a mortgage company. If your lender escrows, send them your copy.

sections.h2: When are Pike County property taxes due and what happens after?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property bills are due December 1. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1, and the office accepts a United States Postal Service postmark but not a metered one.

After the due date, interest is added on the 2nd of each month at prime plus 3% divided by 12. A 5% penalty lands after 120 days and again every 120 days, stopping at 20%. A mobile home that misses April 1 draws a 10% penalty on April 2.

If the bill stays unpaid, the office files a FIFA with the Clerk of Superior Court 30 days after the date on the delinquent notice. A later stage sends the account to a collection contractor, and administrative and levy fees of up to $215 plus are added to cover certified notices and a title search. The property is then posted, photographed and advertised in the local newspaper for four weeks before a sale.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Pike County assessment?
sections.html:
File a written appeal with the Pike County Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the date on your assessment notice. Late appeals are not accepted.

The appeal can argue the taxability of the property, its value, or whether that value is uniform with similar properties in the county. It cannot argue that the tax itself is too high. If the assessors do not agree, the file moves to the Board of Equalization, and the owner may choose arbitration instead. The next step after that is Superior Court.

Pike's page adds two details that matter to some owners. A mobile home owner who disputes value has 45 days with the assessors and then 21 days to go to the Board of Equalization. An owner away on armed forces duty can have a friend or relative file within 90 days of the notice of value.

sections.h2: Which Pike County exemptions can lower the bill?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one. You must own and occupy the home on January 1, apply at the assessor's office, and have the application in before April 1 to count for that tax year.

  • First-time applicants should bring a copy of the warranty deed.
  • Pike has local county homestead exemptions, and a local amount replaces the state amount whenever it is larger.
  • Owners who reach age 62 can apply for an additional homestead exemption.
  • Agricultural property can be assessed at 30% of fair market value instead of 40%, and conservation use property is assessed at current use value. Both require a covenant of at least 10 years and an application by April.
  • Manufacturers can ask for the freeport exemption between January 1 and April 1.

Once granted, the homestead exemption renews each year. A move, an ownership change or a request for a different exemption means a new application.

sections.h2: How does Pike County turn a value into a bill?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes 40% of fair market value, and Pike's tax commissioner explains the rest in order. Start with the assessed value, subtract any exemption to reach the net taxable value, then multiply by the millage rate. One mill equals $1 for each $1,000 of assessed value.

The Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education set the rates each year, and the tax bill lists both fair market value and assessed value. Returns matter too. A real estate return is due between January 1 and April 1 when property has changed hands or been improved, and skipping a required return brings a 10% penalty on the value not returned. Personal property, such as business equipment, needs a new return every year.

Georgia's Department of Revenue adds that a refund request for tax wrongly collected must start within three years of payment.

sections.h2: How should I sell a Pike County house that owes tax?
sections.html:
Settle the bill at closing, and start by asking the tax commissioner for the exact balance, since interest is added monthly. A buyer's title search will find any FIFA recorded against the property, so a lien does not stay hidden.

  1. Call (770) 567-2001 and request the current amount, including interest and any penalty.
  2. Check whether a FIFA has been filed, and ask what is needed to clear it.
  3. If the account has gone to the collection stage, ask for the added fees in writing.
  4. Confirm who owes the current year's bill, since tax is set by owner and value on January 1.
  5. Have the closing attorney pay each balance from your proceeds.

A sale before the account reaches the tax sale stage avoids the advertising and levy costs. An as-is cash buyer can close around those costs, and the payoff is handled from the proceeds like any other lien.

faqs.q: Is the Pike County tax bill due December 1 or December 20?
faqs.a: December 1. The Pike County tax commissioner's site states that real estate and business personal property are due December 1, and Georgia's Department of Revenue notes that the statewide default of December 20 can be changed by the local government.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Pike County?
faqs.a: Interest of prime plus 3% divided by 12 is added monthly, and a 5% penalty applies after 120 days and every 120 days after that, up to 20%. Mobile homes get a flat 10% penalty on April 2.

faqs.q: Where do I file a homestead exemption in Pike County?
faqs.a: At the Pike County Tax Assessor's office, with the application received by April 1. Bring your warranty deed if you recently bought the home.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Pike County house if a tax lien has been filed?
faqs.a: Yes. The FIFA is paid from the sale proceeds at closing. Ask the tax commissioner at (770) 567-2001 for the payoff and for what they need to release the lien.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Pike County property value?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors at (770) 567-2002. The tax commissioner at (770) 567-2001 handles billing and payment, not value.
